A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OmniEVA. Their complete main texts and appendices support comparison of methods, equations, experiments, tables and figures despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, simulated navigation and manipulation results, reward ablations, and qualitative robot deployments.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds fusion comparisons, embodiment-generalization experiments, quantitative real-robot evaluations, and dynamic-occlusion cases.

M1.justification: The hard TAGR gate, additive 3D fusion, training losses and TE-GRPO reward curriculum remain unchanged. The explicitly named three-stage pipeline was already represented in v1's pretraining description and Table 5; additional implementation details and Base/ER checkpoint names do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: The training corpus and established benchmarks are retained. v3 substantially extends embodied test scenarios through unseen physical configurations, two real robot platforms instead of single-platform demonstrations, explicit cluttered-picking and constrained-navigation evaluations, and moving-pedestrian occlusion cases (Section 4.3 and Appendix B.3).

E2.justification: Table 1 adds separate-token cross-attention, interleaved-token cross-attention, and continuous soft gating to the existing hard-coded and no-3D comparisons. These substantially broaden the alternatives evaluated against the central routing mechanism. Comparator membership in Tables 2–4 is unchanged.

E3.justification: New experiments train on 75, 88 and 110 cm arms and evaluate seven held-out lengths, while real-robot comparisons report ten attempts per model/task/embodiment. Gate analysis changes from frequent-word statistics to whole-prompt semantic categorization with specified similarity thresholds (Appendix C.2). Retained benchmark settings are largely unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds tests of alternative fusion mechanisms, generalization to unseen embodiments, and robustness to moving occluders. It replaces word-level gate analysis with semantic-category analysis. Existing reward ablations and several qualitative cases are retained or relocated rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports multi-seed variability, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new ten-attempt robot evaluations specify sample sizes, rather than introducing uncertainty estimation or repeated-training-run reporting.

E6.justification: v3 adds fusion-comparator scores, semantic gate-activation results, and Tables 5–6: ER achieves 80.52% success on unseen arm lengths and 9/10 placement successes on both robots. Navigation is 8/10 versus Base's 9/10 and 8/10, so improvements are not universal. Tables 2–4 and the original reward-ablation scores remain unchanged. Table 1's reported dynamic-fusion average changes from 58.56 to 58.7, beyond equivalent rounding.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation of TAGR, reward composition, normalized advantages and GRPO optimization is retained; the latter equations move to Appendix A.3. Added implementation and analysis pseudocode does not introduce a new theoretical result or proof.

C1.justification: Both versions claim task-adaptive 3D grounding, embodiment-aware reasoning, four primitive benchmarks, leading performance on seven of eight public benchmarks, and strong downstream planning. v3 makes the abstract more explicit but does not materially redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations involving positional-encoding amplitude and cross-attention learning difficulties, plus explicit limitations concerning scene-level gating and unmodeled physical parameters. It also interprets unseen-embodiment and dynamic-obstruction results. Conversely, v1's specific explanation that grasp-controller limitations constrain Mobile Pickup gains is removed.

D1.justification: Appendix A substantially expands implementation disclosure with mixed RGB/RGB-D preprocessing, depth masking, forward-pass listings, reward-computation pseudocode, temperature scheduling and eight-candidate GRPO groups. v3 also specifies backbone resetting after router pretraining and promises code/data release. However, v1's explicit KL weight of 0.01 is omitted; actual resource availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v3 adds the DeepSeek-R1 reference for its language-editing disclosure in Appendix H. The substantive related-work coverage and positioning against embodied-reasoning and 3D-language-model research remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, training exposition and experimental narrative are extensively revised. Training receives explicit stage and checkpoint labels; benchmark descriptions and case studies are reorganized into appendices. Dedicated limitations, reproducibility and LLM-use sections are added.

P2.justification: Figure 4 changes from word-level activation bars to a semantic-category chart, and Table 1 gains grouped fusion comparisons. New embodiment and robot-result tables, dynamic-obstruction and fusion diagrams, algorithms and code listings substantially expand the presentation. Existing case studies and benchmark illustrations are also relocated.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens validation of both central contributions: Table 1 tests meaningful fusion alternatives, while Tables 5–6 supplement v1's qualitative physical demonstrations with held-out-embodiment and comparative real-robot results. Expanded implementation disclosure also improves assessability. These gains outweigh the removed grasp-controller caveat and numerical inconsistencies, although ten-attempt robot tests without uncertainty estimates still limit the strength of deployment conclusions.
